user_request: Keep autonomous development repairable without weakening the final acceptance boundary. A drift detector may warn during the repair loop, but the project must not become claimable as ready unless an authoritative acceptance path fails closed on the same material drift.

known_evidence: A project-level control-plane drift detector exists and returns non-zero when authority mirrors or stale control state diverge.
The detector was originally attached to an agent lifecycle hook as a hard failure; this made the same agent repair loop vulnerable to being blocked by the defect it needed to fix.
The lifecycle hook was changed to emit a warning so the agent can continue repairing the repository.
No authoritative readiness, acceptance, release, or merge-control path is currently proven to execute that detector fail-closed after repair.

Local developer or agent hooks are not equivalent to repository acceptance enforcement: local hooks may be bypassable or intentionally advisory, while protected-branch required checks are the mechanism that actually prevents merge when configured.
unknowns: Which existing acceptance owner is the correct place to run the detector without creating a second control plane.
Whether repository governance is authorized to make the resulting status check required.

scoring_focus: diagnostics at a repair-time control point must not make the defect impossible to repair
advisory repair-time checks cannot substitute for fail-closed acceptance of the finished state
the same material invariant should be owned by an existing authoritative validation path rather than duplicated into another scheduler or control plane
merge-policy or branch-protection changes remain explicit repository-governance decisions
zero-cost local validation is preferred and hosted CI must not be triggered merely to prove the topology
